item.title: The Hadamard Gate: Quantum's 45-Degree Turn
item.description: The Hadamard gate is the foundation of every quantum algorithm—it transforms certainty into superposition. But here's the insight most tutorials miss: applying a Hadamard to your qubit is mathematically equivalent to rotating your measurement device by 45 degrees. Through polarized sunglasses analogies and Qiskit code, discover why 'rotating the particle' and 'rotating the detector' are two sides of the same quantum coin.

item.title: Mutation Testing: How to Know If Your Tests Actually Work
item.description: Code coverage tells you which lines your tests execute, but not whether they verify anything meaningful. Mutation testing introduces deliberate bugs to check if your tests catch them. Learn how AST parsing enables robust code transformations and why a 95% coverage score might be lying to you.

item.title: Debugging Python in Docker Containers with Doom Emacs
item.description: Take your Doom Emacs debugging skills into Docker containers. Learn how to set up remote debugging with debugpy, configure path mappings, and debug Flask, Django, and Celery applications running in containers—all with the same DAP workflow you know and love.

item.title: Debugging Python in Doom Emacs with LSP and DAP
item.description: Master debugging in Doom Emacs using the Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) with LSP integration. Learn how to set breakpoints, step through code, inspect variables, and use the REPL to debug Python programs without leaving your favorite editor.

item.title: The CNOT Gate: Building Quantum Twins with Bell States
item.description: Explore the CNOT gate—the workhorse of quantum circuits—and discover how combining it with superposition creates Bell states, the simplest examples of quantum entanglement. Through relatable analogies like copycat friends, dancing partners, and magical correlated coins, learn why Einstein called entanglement "spooky action at a distance" and see it in action with Qiskit code examples.

item.title: Quantum Measurement for Software Developers
item.description: Understanding quantum measurement is crucial for developers working with quantum computing. This guide explains how the outcome of measuring a quantum particle depends entirely on the measuring device's configuration, without getting into complex math. Learn how quantum states work, why measurement creates outcomes, and see practical examples using Qiskit.

item.title: Introduction to Quantum Computing
item.description: Quantum computing represents one of the most exciting frontiers in modern technology. Unlike classical computers that use bits as the smallest unit of information (0 or 1), quantum computers use quantum bits or qubits, which can exist in multiple states simultaneously. This fundamental difference opens up possibilities for solving certain problems exponentially faster than traditional computers...

item.title: Building Modern Web Applications
item.description: In today's rapidly evolving tech landscape, building modern web applications requires a combination of cutting-edge technologies and well-established best practices. Learn how to create robust, scalable, and maintainable web applications by choosing the right technology stack, following key development principles, and incorporating emerging technologies like WebAssembly and serverless architectures.

item.title: Web Development Trends in 2025
item.description: As we progress further into 2025, the web development landscape continues to evolve at a rapid pace. New technologies, frameworks, and methodologies are emerging that promise to reshape how we build and interact with web applications. In this article, I'll explore the most significant trends shaping the future...

item.title: Creative CSS Techniques
item.description: CSS has evolved far beyond simple styling rules. Modern CSS offers incredible capabilities for creating stunning visual effects and animations that were previously only possible with heavy JavaScript libraries or even Flash. In this article, I'll share some of my favorite creative CSS techniques...
